question: Must the intention for a fast be made before Fajr, or can it be made later in the day?
asked: For fard or for nafl fasting, can the intention be made up until midday if I didn't make it before dawn? And the same goes for qada: does the intention have to be made before dawn, or can I make it up until midday?
answer:
Okay, so for the fard and for the qada of the fard. Right, so you have some fasts you have to make up from last Ramadan, and you have to make them up before this Ramadan. By the way, if you haven't done that, please do that; it's very important. In case you do not do that before this Ramadan, then there is a bit of a sin on you, but I mean, not a major sin. But still, it's something that's makruh; I should say not a sin, but it is makruh. And make it up as soon as you can after this Ramadan finishes. You don't want to pile it up. You should get rid of the debt to Allah as fast as possible.

But when you are making up qada, and when you are fasting the fard fast of Ramadan, you must have had the niyyah before Salat al-Fajr, before the adhan of Fajr. Now, this does not mean that you have to wake up at 4am every single day. Right now Ramadan is going to come; in your heart is the niyyah for the entire month. That is good enough. And so if a day comes when you wake up at... so the Fajr adhan is coming in at, let's say, 5:40. Suppose you wake up at 6:20 one day and you're like, "Oh my god, I didn't have the intention." No, you have the intention, because we all have the intention to fast the entire month of Ramadan, and that is good enough. So you need to have the intention before the adhan of Fajr, and **a generic intention for the entire month is good enough.**

However, if it is a nafl fast, you just want to fast because it's an act of worship, nafl fasts are much easier. And with a nafl fast, you can decide to fast in the middle of the day, or even, frankly, after this. Some scholars said in the middle of the day, and some said even after this, and that is the stronger position, because there's no evidence to restrict it to the middle of the day: that if you decide to fast at 11am, at noon, at 1pm, at 3pm. But obviously there's one important condition, and frankly very few of us meet that condition. That condition is we should not have eaten or drunk anything since the Fajr adhan. So by 4pm, how many amongst us would not even have had a sip of water? Think about that.

But suppose somebody wakes up, they pray Fajr, they go back to sleep. They wake up at, let's say, 11 o'clock. "Okay, I had a long night," and they just go to sleep after Fajr, and wake up at 11 or even noon, and they're like, "Oh, it's already 11:30, only six hours left or seven hours left. Might as well fast." No problem, as long as they haven't taken a sip of water or even a morsel of food from the time of Fajr. And they can make the niyyah to fast a nafl fast any time of the day. No problem. But not the fard, and not the qada of the fard, because innamal a'malu bin-niyyat. And when you want to do a fard, that is a higher level, and you have to have the niyyah from the beginning of the fast. And Allah 'azza wa jall knows best.
